$comment: What this release of Kanon needs of an adopter (plan 0005 §5.4, §5.5), read at the release's tag. Built from the lanes by tests/unit/requirements.test.ts, which fails when this file and the lanes disagree; rebuild it with KANON_WRITE_REQUIREMENTS=1 npx vitest run tests/unit/requirements.test.ts. `kanon init` writes callers, the hook and the App identities from it; `kanon doctor` checks an installation against a release's copy. `identities` are the names a lane's `<NAME>_APP_ID` secret carries: a role of rulebook/agent-permissions.json today, an App of it once the lanes take the Apps' secrets. `catalogue` is the lane catalogue, copied from docs/lanes.json.

apply.description: 'true' to actually re-dispatch on a dispatch (anything else = dry run)

tier.description: The tier to sweep, as the adopter's sweep hook names them; empty sweeps every tier.

reset.description: Clear the round cap for this run. Use when the developer has resolved the disagreement the cap escalated — that is a new instruction, not a third iteration of the same argument. Authorises exactly one revision.

project.description: Tracking issue number of the project (blank = every open project)

apply.description: 'true' to actually file and dispatch on a dispatch (anything else = dry run)

reset.description: Clear the round cap for this run. Use when the developer has ANSWERED the brief's open decisions — that is a new mandate, not a third iteration of a disagreement. Authorises exactly one revision.

issue.description: The oversized issue to split (it must carry qa:needs-split)

mandate.description: What to plan — one paragraph, in your own words

pr_number.description: A single PR to consider (blank = sweep every open PR)

apply.description: 'true' to actually merge, comment and label on a dispatch (anything else = report only)

dry_run.description: 'true' to print the message instead of posting it, and file nothing

pr_number.description: A single PR to consider (blank = every open PR)

project.description: Project tracking-issue number (the brief is docs/projects/<n>.md)

ref.description: Tag or SHA to verify; empty for the default branch

week_end.description: End of the 7-day window (ISO date). Defaults to now.

dry_run.description: 'true' to print the message instead of posting it

agent-review.name: Review
agent-review.does: Reviews each pull request once CI finishes on its head, and approves it or requests changes.
needs: your CI at `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, whose runs it reads
agent-review.cost: A model run per reviewed head.
agent-review.when: Always, and first: its App's approval is what ends bootstrap (`K-ADOPT-6`).

agent-merge-reconcile.name: Merge reconcile
agent-merge-reconcile.does: After a reviewed pull request merges, files a follow-up issue for each review suggestion it didn't apply.
agent-merge-reconcile.cost: A model run per merged pull request the Reviewer reviewed.
agent-merge-reconcile.when: When the Reviewer's suggestions that a merge left out should become issues rather than be lost.

agent-implement.name: Implement
agent-implement.does: Builds a feature or resolves a spec delta from an issue labelled `agent:implement`, and opens a pull request.
agent-implement.cost: A model run per labelled issue.
agent-implement.when: When you want agents to write code from the issues you label, once the Reviewer runs green.

agent-implement-revise.name: Implement, revise
agent-implement-revise.does: Revises the Implementer's own pull request when the Reviewer requests changes.
agent-implement-revise.cost: A model run per change request, capped in rounds.
agent-implement-revise.when: With implement: without it, a change request on the Implementer's pull request waits for a person.

agent-explore.name: Explore (the sweep)
agent-explore.does: Sweeps your running product with a sweep hook you write, and files what it finds.
agent-explore.cost: A model run daily, skipped on a commit the QA store already holds a green sweep of.
agent-explore.when: When you can write a sweep hook that exercises your product, such as a Playwright run.

agent-code-audit.name: Code audit
agent-code-audit.does: Reads your code and specs every few days, and files a bug only on an objective contradiction.
agent-code-audit.cost: A model run every three days.
agent-code-audit.when: When you want a periodic second reading of the code, guided by `## Code areas` in your stack document.

agent-explore-telemetry.name: Explore the telemetry
agent-explore-telemetry.does: Reads Kanon's hosted telemetry aggregate weekly, never a row, and files or drafts the anomalies it finds in Kanon's lanes: failures by lane, stage, error and Kanon version, and costs per lane and model.
needs: an aggregate invoker role from Kanon's telemetry register (`aggregate_invoker`), whose ARN is the secret `KANON_AGGREGATE_ROLE`, and the repository variable `KANON_AGGREGATE_URL` (docs/telemetry.md)
agent-explore-telemetry.cost: A model run weekly, skipped when the aggregate holds no cell and no signal.
agent-explore-telemetry.when: When your telemetry register entry has an aggregate invoker role, so you can read the aggregate.

agent-triage.name: Triage and fix
agent-triage.does: Reproduces a bug labelled `qa:needs-triage`, rates it, and proposes a fix as a pull request.
agent-triage.cost: A model run per labelled issue.
agent-triage.when: When you file bugs for the agents to fix, or with explore or the code audit, whose findings it triages.

agent-lead.name: Lead, brief
agent-lead.does: Turns a mandate you dispatch into a project brief, opened as a pull request.
needs: project briefs under `docs/projects/`, from the brief template (`K-PROJ-1`)
agent-lead.when: When you want agents to plan work that spans several issues.

agent-lead-revise.name: Lead, revise
agent-lead-revise.does: Revises the Lead's own brief pull request when the Reviewer requests changes.
agent-lead-revise.cost: A model run per change request, capped in rounds.
agent-lead-revise.when: With the Lead's brief: without it, a change request on a brief waits for a person.

agent-lead-split.name: Lead, split
agent-lead-split.does: Proposes splitting a project issue too big for one Implementer run, as a pull request against its brief.
agent-lead-split.cost: A model run per labelled issue.
agent-lead-split.when: With the Lead's brief, so an issue too big for one run is split rather than stalled.

agent-lead-reconcile.name: Lead, reconcile
agent-lead-reconcile.does: Drives an approved brief to done: files its issues, labels them for the Implementer in order, and closes the project once its merges are deployed.
agent-lead-reconcile.cost: No model; a short job on each merge and an hourly heartbeat.
agent-lead-reconcile.when: With the Lead's brief: it is what turns an approved brief into work.

agent-verify-acs.name: Verify acceptance criteria
agent-verify-acs.does: Runs the tests that cite a project's acceptance criteria, and has the Explorer file what fails.
agent-verify-acs.cost: A model run per project verified.
agent-verify-acs.when: With the reconciler, which asks it to verify a project before closing it.

agent-overseer.name: Overseer (optional)
agent-overseer.does: Audits the pipeline weekly from its aggregate, and again when a Kanon upgrade moves the agent runtime past its capability ledger's watermark, and files what you can act on as `pipeline-improvement` issues.
agent-overseer.cost: A model run weekly, plus one when a Kanon upgrade moves the agent runtime forward. Every other merged Kanon upgrade runs only a short gate job.
agent-overseer.when: Once you run the Implementer, the Lead or the Merger unattended: it audits what runs without you watching (a lane that stopped, fixes that game their tests, follow-ups that leak, configuration drift, the cost trend). With only the Reviewer, or lanes you trigger by hand, you see every run anyway, and its first audits say little until weeks of history exist.

agent-project-digest.name: Daily project digest
agent-project-digest.does: Posts each open project's progress to a chat channel daily, and files an issue for a lane caller that keeps failing.
agent-project-digest.when: With the reconciler, when you have a chat channel for the developers.

agent-weekly-digest.name: Weekly digest
agent-weekly-digest.does: Posts the week's burndown and deliveries in plain language to a chat channel, for a stakeholder outside the day-to-day work.
agent-weekly-digest.when: When the Stakeholder is not the Owner and follows the project from outside, through a chat channel.

agent-merge.name: Merge
agent-merge.does: Merges, with no person, an Implementer pull request the Reviewer approved with every check green, inside the green zone (`K-MERGE-4`).
agent-merge.cost: No model; a short job per review, per CI run on the default branch, and hourly.
agent-merge.when: Once you have merged the Implementer's approved pull requests by hand for a while, and trust the green zone.
agent-merge.mergeQueue: Through a merge queue, a merge doesn't start its sweep: the queue's push runs CI as `github-merge-queue[bot]`, which the lane's gate turns away, so it sweeps on a review and hourly (#79).

agent-rebase.name: Rebase (resolve a conflict)
agent-rebase.does: Resolves a merge conflict on an agent's pull request, so its CI and review can resume.
agent-rebase.cost: A model run per conflicting agent pull request, checked on each CI run and daily.
agent-rebase.when: With implement or triage, whose pull requests otherwise wait for a person when they conflict: a person's rebase takes one out of the Implementer's chain, so the revise lane refuses it.

agent-dispatch-sweep.name: Dispatch sweep
agent-dispatch-sweep.does: Re-dispatches, once a day, an implement or triage run that never happened, and reports what waits on a person.
agent-dispatch-sweep.cost: No model; a short job daily.
agent-dispatch-sweep.when: With implement or triage, so a label whose event never arrived still starts its run.
